What is the purpose of interrupts? What are the differences between a trap and an interrupt? Can traps be generated intentionally by a user program? If so, for what purpose?
questions.answer: An interrupt is an electrical signal sent from one component of the computer to another, signaling that an event has occurred which requires immediate action by the component receiving the interrupt. A trap is a specific type of interrupt which is generated by software and signals either 1.some unusual condition, such as an array index out of bounds, or 2.a request for an operating system service (a system call.) User program scan generate traps, although not all high-level programming languages make this facility directly available to the programmer. (Ada, C and Java do allow the programmer to generate traps. Traps are called “exceptions” in Ada and Java, and “signals” in C. In addition, C allows programmers to bypass the API and make system calls directly.) Traps are used to notify the CPU that some unusual software event has taken place, or that some special service has been requested by the program. The CPU can then either terminate the program, or interrupt the normal execution sequence of the program and transfer control to a special segment of code.

questions.question_text: Describe the advantage of DMA transfer with neat diagram
questions.answer:
Advantages:
• They improve the overall performance of the whole system. The processor will have more time to execute other processes.
• They reduce CPU overhead when data is being transferred. Most of the overhead work is left to the DMA controller.
• CPU and DMA work concurrently. DMA will be transferring data while the CPU is executing.
• Increase the speed of data transfer from the main memory to the I/O module

(Diagram illustrates the DMA architecture showing the CPU with thread of execution and cache, instruction execution cycle and data movement connected to memory, and DMA controller handling data transfer directly between the device and memory with I/O request, data, and interrupt lines).

questions.question_text:
Which network configuration (LAN or WAN) would best suit the following environments? Give Justification.
• A campus student union
• Several campus locations across a statewide university system
• A neighborhood
questions.answer:
• A campus student union consists of computers connected together which are in a specific area inside the campus, probably connecting offices in several buildings. Thus LAN is suitable.
• Several campus locations across a statewide university system – It covers larger areas and even allow computers in different states. Thus WAN is suitable for this.
• Neighborhood – It may be a particular part of a town or it can be township. So, we can use either LAN or WAN

questions.question_text: Describe some of the challenges of designing operating systems for mobile devices compared with designing operating systems for traditional PCs.
questions.answer:
• Mobile devices are a great technological advance, which establishes great practicality and comfort.
• However, their operating system is still limited compared to the computer operating system.
• This limitation is directly related to the storage capacity and the "power" to run some types of software.
• Mobile devices have very low storage capacity, which can lead to user dissatisfaction and malfunctions

questions.question_text:
Design a file-copying program named filecopy using ordinary pipes. This program will be passed two parameters: the name of the file to be copied and the name of the copied file. The program will then create an ordinary pipe and write the contents of the file to be copied to the pipe. The child process will read this file from the pipe and write it to the destination file. For example, if we invoke the program as follows:
```
filecopy input.txt copy.txt
```
The file input.txt will be written to the pipe. The child process will read the contents of this file and write it to the destination file copy.txt. You may write this program using either Linux or Windows pipes.
